description: Check in one call whether LPF covers a brand, model, or part type at all, before you search. Use list_models instead to page through models. Use get_model_parts instead for a model's part numbers. Use resolve_request or search_parts instead to find a specific part. Default (summary omitted or false): totals, brands, part types, and every model with its part types and fit counts (~1 MB). summary true: the same without the models list (models_omitted gives the count; ~6 KB) — prefer for brand or part-type questions; use full mode only to look up a specific model. Snapshot at deploy time: generated is the build date; data_revision changes when data or server changes. Not listed means no documented fit, not incompatibility.

summary.description: Optional, default false. true omits the per-model list (same as REST /api/coverage?summary=1).

name: get_coverage

fit_status.description: no_documented_fit: there is no fit or no result: LPF has no OEM document for it. Never means incompatible. not_asserted: a did-you-mean suggestion; no fit claim is made.

outcome.description: Always present. One field to branch on for every tool: found | no_documented_fit (identified, but no OEM-documented fit; never means incompatible) | needs_clarification (ask the user; see clarifying_question/candidates) | not_found (nothing LPF covers matches). Full contract: /api/states

title: Get coverage manifest
